name: Hover Morph Distortion
summary: A shader-driven liquid warp liquefies the hero photograph under the cursor — displacement trails the pointer path with viscous, damped follow, and warp intensity scales with cursor velocity. The layout never moves; motion lives entirely inside the image plane while type and subject cutouts stay razor-sharp.

composition: A stable graphic anchor is mandatory: a giant flat display word and/or a crisp cutout subject that the liquefying photo plays against.
The distortion zone is the full photographic plane; clipping it to a small hover target wastes the effect.
Small supporting label/CTA anchored low keeps the frame quiet.
layering: Three planes with strict roles: background photo plate (DEFORMS) → giant flat type (STABLE) → foreground cutout subject (STABLE, occludes type).
Because only one plane deforms, the warp reads as intentional craft rather than glitch — corrupt everything and it reads as error.
The ripple can read as wet-glass refraction: displacement plus slight magnification near the pointer.
lighting: Soft high-key daylight photography (airy skies, no hard shadows) shows displacement most clearly — busy dark imagery hides the warp.
No glows or vignettes: clarity over drama; the type provides graphic 'light' via a pure saturated fill.
typography: Heavy geometric display sans at poster scale, single weight, tight; tiny tracked uppercase captions.
Type itself does NOT animate — the image does; the contrast between liquid photo and frozen type is the aesthetic.

rules: Neutral desaturated photographic base + ONE loud saturated hue owning the type — the accent is the brand voice; everything else stays muted so the morph reads clearly.

easing: Viscous damped follow — the distortion LAGS the cursor and relaxes back slowly (~0.6-1s decay); no snap, no bounce.
Warp intensity maps to cursor VELOCITY: fast sweeps tear, slow drifts gently swell.
pacing: Continuous and ambient while the pointer moves; fully at rest when idle — unlike fluid/particle fields, this family is silent until touched.
Decay must complete before the image fully re-sharpens; an instant reset breaks the liquid illusion.
choreography: Pointer position is the sole driver — no autoplay, no scroll binding.
Only the photographic layer responds; subject cutout and headline hold, giving the eye a stable reference for the deformation.

gapNotes: A TSL displacement shader on a textured plane is native territory, but the pointer-velocity-to-warp-intensity driver (with viscous lag and decay) is not a shipped primitive — displacement-transition is a one-shot transition, not a continuous pointer field.
Needs the cutout pipeline (W-PHOTO) for the stable-subject sandwich: FLUX image → background-removed cutout + intact photo plate.

whenToUse: Creative/portfolio/fashion heroes needing tactile GPU craft with a calm idle state (unlike always-moving fields).
Image-led brands where photography quality is high and deserves to be 'touchable'.
whenNotToUse: Touch-first/mobile-heavy audiences — the effect is pointer-dependent and invisible on tap devices without a designed fallback.
Text-dense or data-heavy pages; per-frame displacement is a battery/jank risk on weak GPUs.
Brands wanting institutional restraint — liquefying imagery reads experimental.

notes: Shares the pointer-reactive-field cluster: never combine two pointer-driven GPU effects — the cursor can only author one field at a time.

antiRepetition.notes: Same cluster as gpu-fluid-overlay and particle-field-hero.

sources.title: Hover Morph Effect Hero Collection
sources.motionEvidence: Founder monitor session, live demo: cursor swept at varied velocities — velocity-scaled tearing vs gentle swelling observed; decay-to-rest timed; stability of type and cutout planes during deformation confirmed across collection variants.
